target_paper.title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty
target_paper.original_source: Table 6 (no-CoT) and Table 5 (CoT) rows for gpt-4.1-nano, MedQA

generation.battery: 4 dataset variants x zero-shot x {no-CoT, CoT (NA/A/AP)} = 7,049 calls; accuracy on the 70% test split after the 30% calibration split (seed 42)

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN §1; human double-coding pending
results.note: All seven accuracy rows reproduce (originals inside the 95% CIs; largest gap NAP 0.4255 vs 0.4511). The 'never abstains' claim holds only approximately: 2.5% (A) and 3.2% (AP) of test items pick the abstention option without CoT, 14% under the CoT prompt (paper: 0.0). Conformal set sizes deviate by 0.2-0.5 options in both directions; they depend on the exact logprob values and the calibration split.

reproducibility_frictions_observed: original runs went through the openai SDK with model alias 'gpt-4.1-nano'; the dated snapshot is named only in Appendix E
calibration/test split is seeded in utils.load_and_split_jsonl (random_state 42) although the card had recorded it as unseeded
few-shot conditions require text-embedding-ada-002 kNN demonstrations (out of scope here)
the CoT prompt with max_tokens=1 is a protocol artifact the paper reports as Table 5; reproduced as such
